newsitem.title: USA: HFS says EPS growth 25-30 pct/yr achievable.
newsitem.headline: HFS says EPS growth 25-30 pct/yr achievable.

text.p: HFS Inc chairman Henry Silverman said a 25 to 30 percent annual growth rate in per share earnings is "achievable".
HFS is the world's largest hotel franchiser. It also owns Avis car rental company, PHH Corp and Century 21.

Silverman, speaking at a gathering of financial journalists here, declined to specifically comment on Wall Street's earnings forecast, but said, "In five years we have never disappointed on EPS."1 According to First Call, the consensus forecast for HFS's 1997 earnings is $2.66 per share versus $1.34 earned in 1996.

In response to a question, Silverman said the company is primarily interested in acquiring a company in the "direct response marketing business" in order to leverage HFS's growing database of customers culled from the company's real estate- and travel-related businesses.
"We have a data warehouse with about 19 million names in it, and it is growing by about two million names a month," Silverman said.
